note: Candidates that exercise the empirical constraints E2, E3, E4 and E7. Every elimination here is CONDITIONAL on the observation named in the row (conditionalOn in the ledger): a reader who rejects the observation drops the elimination, and the arithmetic is kernel-checked either way. Sources: physics/length-weight.csv (the fitted mass-exponent band), physiology/ through lean/eliminate/physiology-candidates.json (the measured teleost ranges and the oxycaloric equivalent), physics/glide-data.csv and the physics thread's flier spec (the power required), genotype/interventions.json (the two lethal levers the genotype thread states in hours). E1 (isometry fails), E5 (the measured fin-ratio range) and E6 (the propagation convention) deliberately have no constraint: E1 is the hypothesis behind the audit's violated rows, E5 is a provenance flag in the Design Studio, and E6 is a project convention.
label: candidates for the empirical layer: what the project's own measurements rule out, each conditional on a stated observation

candidates.problem: May a design take the H. affinis male exponent as the family's mass exponent?
candidates.description: A design committing a mass exponent of 2.208, the male-only Hirundichthys affinis row, as if it were a fit of the family. Every other fitted row lies in [2.908, 3.011].
candidates.source: physics/length-weight.csv (H. affinis male, n=117, TL, Caicara do Norte 2011-2012)

candidates.description: Cheilopogon unicolor, b = 2.971 over n = 1640, inside the band by construction.

candidates.problem: Could ANY teleost in the measured ranges sustain the real fish's flight?
candidates.description: Level flight of the Park and Choi specimen at its measured maximum lift-to-drag ratio needs 1.3473 W (W 0.5886 N at 10 m/s with L/D 4.37, the most generous reading). The question is not whether the chain's particular proxies can pay for it, but whether any teleost inside the measured ranges can.
candidates.source: physics/glide-data.csv (Park and Choi 2010 model L3) for the power required; physiology/ for the ranges

candidates.problem: Control: a claim small enough to pass the ceiling
candidates.description: A sustained aerobic power of 0.04 W, below the 0.0458 W ceiling the measured ranges allow at 0.06 kg. Consistent, which says only that the oxygen budget is not what rules it out.

candidates.problem: Could a minute of powered flight be paid for out of the O2 store?
candidates.description: Sixty seconds of level flight at 1.3473 W with 1 ml O2 carried into the air at 19.342857 J/ml. The store is illustrative: no blood volume or venous reserve is measured for Exocoetidae in this project.
candidates.source: physiology/muscle.js for the oxycaloric equivalent; the store is illustrative; the power is the Park and Choi specimen at L/D 4.37

candidates.problem: Control: a two-second burst on the same store
candidates.description: The same store and power over 2 s, which the store covers (the model allows it; the fish is understood to burst on white muscle, which this bound does not describe).

candidates.problem: May a design use ezh2 loss as a lever on fin area?
candidates.description: The genotype thread's own note: 'LETHAL: die around 2 days post fertilization / They die at 48 hpf. The animal dies at the same stage at which the fin phenotype is scored, before any fin skeletal differentiation.'

candidates.problem: May a design use wls loss as a lever on ray length?
candidates.description: The genotype thread's own note: the mutants 'die by approximately 12 dpf' (288 h) while lepidotrichia exist only from Juvenile:Days 45-89 (45 dpf = 1080 h), so no ray length, segment or branching value can be measured in this allele.

candidates.problem: Control: a lever whose animal reaches the stage
candidates.description: The genotype thread records lef1 nl2 as not lethal, with the pectoral lepidotrichium scored in the adult, so the lethality check passes. Adult is taken as 90 dpf = 2160 h for the comparison; death is taken as beyond that and entered as 4320 h, which is a stand-in for 'not reported as lethal' and not a measurement.
